moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how Testim Mobile extends Testim's AI-powered automation to native, hybrid, and cross-platform mobile apps.
Choose between Enhanced mode and Appium mode based on execution and compatibility needs.
Identify the native language support per platform (Android vs. iOS) for recording native apps.

elements.description: Extends Testim's AI-powered test automation — Smart Locators, visual validation, codeless authoring — specifically to mobile app testing, covering native apps, hybrid apps, and cross-platform frameworks.

For Android devices, Testim supports Java or Kotlin native apps; for iOS devices, Objective-C or Swift. Recording works the same way as web — click through the app and Testim captures elements — building toward more stable tests as more application elements are found during recording.

bulletPoints: Testim Mobile = Testim's AI automation (Smart Locators, visual validation) applied to native/hybrid/cross-platform mobile apps.
Android: Java or Kotlin. iOS: Objective-C or Swift.

elements.description: Testim's newer recording/execution mode, designed to be more stable, faster, and more versatile than Appium-based testing. It uses a zero-knowledge approach with a unified API supporting native, hybrid, or cross-platform apps alike. The trade-off: tests recorded in Enhanced mode can only be executed on VMG (Testim's own mobile grid).

Guarantees compatibility with other Appium-based grids and supports local execution on your own local devices. The trade-off runs the other way: it's restricted to Appium's own capabilities, meaning some flows — especially hybrid apps or webviews — may not be fully recordable.

elements.title: Choosing a mode
items: Need maximum stability/speed and are fine executing on VMG only → Enhanced mode.
Need Appium-grid compatibility or local device execution, and can accept Appium's recording limitations → Appium mode.

bulletPoints: Enhanced mode: more stable/faster/versatile, unified API across app types — but VMG-only execution.
Appium mode: Appium-grid compatible + local execution — but limited to what Appium itself can record (hybrid/webviews can be tricky).

examPitfalls.title: Recording in Enhanced mode, then expecting to run on a third-party Appium grid
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a test recorded in Enhanced mode can be executed anywhere, including an external Appium-based grid.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Enhanced mode tests can be executed on VMG only. If execution on an external Appium-based grid or local devices is required, the test must be recorded in Appium mode instead.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to record a hybrid app's webview flow in Appium mode and being surprised by gaps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Hitting recording limitations on a hybrid app/webview scenario while in Appium mode and assuming Testim itself can't handle it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Appium mode is restricted to Appium's own capabilities, which can struggle with hybrid apps or webviews. Enhanced mode's zero-knowledge, unified API is built to handle exactly this case, at the cost of VMG-only execution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which native app languages does Testim Mobile support for recording on Android and iOS respectively?

options.text: Android: Java or Kotlin. iOS: Objective-C or Swift.
Android: Python only. iOS: Java only.
Native app languages are irrelevant to Testim Mobile.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each platform has two supported languages.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For Android devices, Testim supports Java or Kotlin native apps; for iOS devices, it supports Objective-C or Swift.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team needs their mobile tests to run on their own local devices and be compatible with an existing Appium-based grid. Which recording mode should they use?

options.text: Enhanced mode, since it's always the better choice.
Appium mode, since it guarantees Appium-grid compatibility and supports local execution.
Neither mode supports local device execution.
It doesn't matter — both modes are executed identically.

practiceQuiz.hint: One mode is built specifically for Appium-grid and local-device compatibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Appium mode guarantees compatibility with other Appium-based grids and supports local executions on local devices — exactly what this team needs, at the cost of being limited to Appium's own capabilities.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the main execution trade-off of recording a mobile test in Enhanced mode?

options.text: It can only be executed on VMG, Testim's own mobile grid.
It cannot be executed at all, only recorded.
It requires a paid Appium license.
It only works for web apps, not mobile.

practiceQuiz.hint: It trades broad grid compatibility for stability/speed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Enhanced mode tests deliver more stable, faster, more versatile testing than Appium-based testing, but can be executed on VMG only — not on external Appium-based grids or arbitrary local devices.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why might Appium mode struggle to fully record a hybrid app's flow?

options.text: Because Appium mode is restricted to Appium's own capabilities, which can have gaps around hybrid apps and webviews.
Because hybrid apps are not supported by Testim Mobile at all, in any mode.
Because Appium mode only works on iOS.
Because hybrid apps require a separate Testim license.

practiceQuiz.hint: The limitation is about what Appium itself can capture, not about Testim Mobile as a whole.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Appium mode is restricted to Appium's capabilities, meaning some flows may not be fully recordable, especially with hybrid apps or webviews — Enhanced mode's zero-knowledge, unified API is built to handle this case instead.

Java or Kotlin / Objective-C or Swift.
